correctness.rationale: For H,W>=4 integer-valued row/column fields give a universal positive gap 1/(3 max(H,W)) below the largest normalized field; a one-hole state attains this gap. With equal thresholds strictly inside the gap the entire update exactly factors as two argmax support selectors after one step. Symmetry of the three-neighbor matrix makes m(A_t)/|A_t| nondecreasing; constant energy forces A_t subset A_{t+2}. The value lies in at most 3n rational levels, and each constant-energy plateau has at most 2(n-1) strict parity subsequence inclusions before two-periodicity, proving a conservative quadratic bound. Singleton/triple cycles and long-block erosion are exact witnesses. Full proof in RESULT.md and 238104 actual finite checks in verify.py; finite tests are not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The near-one equal-interval model phase has an exact finite-size iff gap, one-step full-matrix rectangular collapse, a global at-most-two period classification and quadratic-time bound. Source 2606.08983 introduced the field model and reported numerical phases, not these results in the accessible original text. The closest inspected published published-finding corpus work establishes a different Rule-54/18 stripe sector with much lower survival/birth thresholds and possible long cycles, not the full-grid near-max selector. Fixed symmetric-threshold theorems of Goles–Olivos assume time-independent site thresholds, and do not directly apply to this global moving-maximum rule. The proof acknowledges the classical reciprocal potential-game principle. Full-text access risk remains recorded, not silently counted as evidence of absence.

value.rationale: The sharp near-max interval is a natural extremal phase of the normalized source model, not an arbitrary unmotivated finite instance. A full two-dimensional, exponentially large state space collapses to rectangles in one iteration; all orbits in this nondegenerate finite-size window have periods at most two and an explicit polynomial settling bound despite linearly long transients. The exact endpoint distinguishes robust max-selection behavior from general interval-threshold dynamics. The result supplies a structural boundary for interpreting the reported multi-periodic phase diagram; no false claim of longer cycles beyond the endpoint is made.
